title: Editorial policy

sections.body: The World of AI is a reference atlas for artificial intelligence, published by SRJ Consulting & Services LLC of Frisco, Texas, and edited by Stephen Jordan. It tracks AI legislation in every state, AI lawsuits in United States courts from their dockets, AI companies, models, tools and research, and it publishes a daily news briefing, a daily record of vendor announcements and a weekly digest of policy and litigation. It is a reference site first and a news site second: pages are built to be read once and cited later, and the news pages exist to show what changed and where the record is.

The daily briefing is compiled, not written by a reporter. Each day the pipeline reads the AI coverage published by several hundred news outlets, clusters the articles that report the same event, and ranks the events by how many independent outlets covered them. Each story page names every outlet and article it was built from, with a link to each, and carries the number of outlets and articles behind it. A short summary is produced from those articles and checked against them; it never adds facts that are not in the coverage. Vendor announcements are taken from each company's own newsroom feed and linked to the original post. The weekly digest is computed from the site's own records of bill movements, Federal Register documents and docket activity, and its opening paragraph is generated from those counts, so it is true by construction.

Every news page shows the date it was compiled and the date of the underlying event, and every story keeps its address permanently at a uid that never changes.

sections.h: Sources and what we do not do
sections.body: We link to primary sources wherever one exists: the bill text, the court docket, the Federal Register notice, the company's own announcement, the paper. We do not reproduce articles, and we do not publish a story that no outlet or primary source supports. Where a page is built from a court docket, it says so and links the docket; where a page is generated from a model's reading of a document, it says so and shows the source the reading was taken from. Nothing on the site is legal, financial or medical advice; the disclaimer says what that means in practice.

sections.h: The role of automation and of the editor
sections.body: Most pages on this site are produced by software from structured records, and some summaries and readings are drafted by a language model working from a named source. The editor sets what is tracked, how it is sourced, which sources are trusted, and the rules the software follows; reviews what the software produces; and is responsible for what is published. Where a page's text was drafted by a model, the page says which one and from what. No page is published from a model's own knowledge without a source, and the site's own question box declines to answer rather than guess.

If something on this site is wrong, tell us at theworldofai@inkboxmail.com or through the contact page, and name the page. A confirmed error in a fact, a date, a case status or a citation is corrected on the page itself, the page's verified date is updated, and where the error was material the correction is noted on the page. We do not silently rewrite. A retired page is never deleted: it is retained with a note saying why, and redirected where a replacement exists. Records, once published, are kept.

The site is free to read and is paid for by advertising, by affiliate commissions on some tool pages, and by the consulting practice that publishes it. No advertiser, affiliate program or sponsor can change a ranking, a legal status, a case summary or a verdict, and the disclosure page sets out what is and is not paid. The editor co-owns an insurance group; the AI Insurance section of this site draws on that experience and says so.

Our own text may be quoted with attribution and a link. Data published through the site's API and downloads carries the licence stated on each; source material linked from our pages belongs to its publishers, and we ask that you cite them, not us, for it.

description: How The World of AI compiles its news, sources its pages, uses automation, corrects errors and is funded.
